properties.name: Tomačevo Bridge
properties.zag_role: Bridge weigh-in-motion and structural health monitoring
properties.description: Elastomeric bearings at the piers and guided unidirectional pot bearings at the abutments. ZAG, Cestel and Dewesoft Monitoring instrumented the bridge for combined bridge weigh-in-motion and structural health monitoring. A controlled load test in May 2024 ran two pre-weighed calibration trucks over 72 passages across two nights, recording strain, acceleration, temperature and displacement at 500 Hz. During normal operation in March 2023 the system captured a 13-axle vehicle weighing over 200 tonnes.
properties.hist: The bridge carries over the Sava north of Ljubljana and is one of the most used routes between the city and its northern suburbs. It is a seven span continuous post tensioned concrete structure of 204 m built in 1982, in two parallel independent decks carrying opposite directions of traffic. The instrumentation combines a Cestel SiWIM bridge weigh in motion system with fourteen triaxial MEMS accelerometers, two strain transducers at main girder mid spans, temperature sensors, displacement transducers and a laser deflection meter, sampling at 500 Hz during controlled testing. For autonomous operation the system can run on two 300 Ah LiFe batteries and four 150 W solar panels.

properties.name: Ravbarkomanda Viaduct
properties.locality: A1 between Planina and Postojna, Postojna
properties.zag_role: Long-term structural health monitoring and bridge weigh-in-motion
properties.description: Two parallel structures carrying one direction each, built in 1972 on what is now the Venice to Lviv corridor. ZAG instrumented span P14D of the right-hand viaduct with strain gauges on the bottom flange of four main girders at mid-span, and triaxial accelerometers across several spans for ambient and traffic-induced modal testing. A bridge weigh-in-motion system supplies the traffic loading, and the measured response is used to update a finite element model of the structure. Both viaducts were fully rehabilitated between May 2017 and June 2019, including carbon fibre strengthening of the cantilevers, bearing replacement and a one metre deck widening.
properties.hist: Ravbarkomanda is a twin multi span precast I girder viaduct on the fifth Trans European corridor, which runs from Venice to Lviv. The right viaduct is about 595 m long with seventeen spans and the left viaduct about 556 m long with fifteen spans, and each carries two lanes and a hard shoulder. The monitoring system installed during the rehabilitation comprises 216 sensors measuring longitudinal strain on main girders, pier caps and deck extensions, temperature sensors across several spans, accelerometers on external prestressing tendons at 24 locations across both viaducts, 40 fibre Bragg grating sensors on carbon fibre rods, and long gauge deformation sensors at six pier cap locations per viaduct. Strain gauges record at 500 samples per second with a 35 Hz low pass filter. The structure crosses a double track railway line and a state road twice.

properties.name: Vransko Bridge
properties.zag_role: Bridge weigh-in-motion measurement and direct measurement of dynamic amplification
properties.description: One of the earliest long SiWIM deployments. Strain was recorded continuously for 58 days, from 25 September to 21 November 2006, capturing 147,524 vehicles including roughly 74,000 five-axle articulated trucks. Total and static bending moments at mid-span were separated to measure the dynamic amplification directly from traffic rather than inferring it from a code factor. The work was done with University College Dublin.
properties.hist: The bridge near Vransko carries the A1 motorway at Brode and has two independent superstructures, one for each travel direction. Each is a simply supported beam and slab structure with a span of 24.8 m between supports, a total length of 26 m, a width of 12 m and no skew. It has been used as a bridge weigh in motion test site with a SiWIM system in the nothing on the road configuration, using ten strain sensors, two per beam, with additional upstream and downstream gauges for axle detection. In the study by O'Brien, González, Dowling and Žnidarič the system ran for 58 days from 25 September to 21 November 2006 and recorded 147,524 vehicles, of which about 74,000 were five axle articulated trucks. The work was part of the European ARCHES project and used the measurements to extract bridge dynamic amplification directly from traffic rather than from controlled runs. The paper states that exact static weights were not available, so no weighing accuracy figure is reported for this deployment.

properties.name: Novo mesto Stress Ribbon Footbridge
properties.zag_role: Static and dynamic load testing in March 2023, in cooperation with dr Andrej Štrukelj (University of Maribor)
properties.description: The first bridge in Slovenia built with stress ribbon technology. ZAG took part in the load test in March 2023, carried out by dr Andrej Štrukelj of the University of Maribor: static loading in three stages, dynamic testing with a light truck driven over artificial obstacles, and ambient vibration measurement. Vertical displacements, natural frequencies and mode shapes were compared against a finite element model and agreed well. Under 18 vehicles with a total mass of 70.4 t the calculated maximum deflection was 145 mm, and the measured values were up to 10 % smaller. Client was the City Municipality of Novo mesto, built by CGP Novo mesto with Freyssinet Adria, designed by Ponting Bridges and Pipenbaher Consulting Engineers.
properties.hist: The footbridge at Irca vas is the first stress ribbon bridge in Slovenia and crosses the Krka between Lastovce and Groblje. Ponting gives a span of 130 m, a width of 4 m and a deck thickness of 42 cm, assembled from 46 precast segments installed on fully tensioned bearing cables between anchored concrete block abutments. Freyssinet describes the same structure with a main span of 120.5 m and six tendons, and states that the grouted tendons are thought to be a first of their kind on this bridge type. The client was the City Municipality of Novo mesto and the contractor was a joint venture of Freyssinet Adria and CGP Novo mesto. The bridge received the Golden Pencil award in 2023 and the Plečnik Medal in 2024, and the City Municipality of Novo mesto refers to it as Štukljeva brv, after the Olympic gymnast Leon Štukelj.

properties.name: Črna na Koroškem Bridge
properties.zag_role: Structural reuse of salvaged girders
properties.description: Demonstration pilot of the CIRCUIT project, planned by the Municipality of Črna na Koroškem with ZAG. A new bridge over the Meža is to reuse the girders of the bridge damaged in the August 2023 floods, with abutments of reinforced soil made from flood deposits, a modular superstructure designed for dismantling and a digitally fabricated safety railing. On 1 October 2025 the bridge was still announced as a future structure, and in June 2026 CIRCUIT reported that the design was still being finalised.
properties.hist: ZAG reported on 26 April 2024 that the bridge will be built in cooperation between the Municipality of Črna na Koroškem and ZAG, after the CIRCUIT consortium visited the site. The local tourist office wrote on 1 October 2025 that the municipality will set up the bridge to link the buildings Center 2 to 4 with the regional road, and presented the project on the Meža bridge at Center 4 on 7 October 2025. The bridge over the Meža opened on 7 September 2025 is a different structure, since the CIRCUIT bridge was still planned after that date.

properties.name: Verd Viaduct
properties.zag_role: First Slovenian application of an expansive grout additive
properties.description: The first structure on which the Ikaton expansive additive was used for grouting prestressing cable ducts. The additive compensates for the shrinkage of cement grout so that the duct fills completely and the tendon is protected from corrosion. Built by Beograjska Mostogradnja. The additive line was developed at ZAG.
properties.hist: The viaduct carries the A1 motorway across the plain at the headwaters of the Ljubljanica near Vrhnika and was built by Beograjska Mostogradnja. It was the first structure on which the Ikaton expansive additive was used for grouting prestressing cable ducts. The additive compensates for the shrinkage of cement grout so that the duct fills completely and the tendon is protected from corrosion, which is one of the principal durability problems in post tensioned concrete bridges.

properties.name: HE Solkan
properties.zag_role: Expansive and non-shrink cements for grout concrete (introduced by ZRMK), technical observation of the dam
properties.description: ZAG's 2024 book states that ZRMK, the predecessor of ZAG, introduced its non-shrink and expansive cements for grout concrete when HE Solkan was built. The same book lists the Solkan dam among the dams under ZAG technical observation.
properties.hist: HE Solkan is the lowest of the large plants on the Soča, standing roughly 700 m upstream of the Solkan railway bridge. It is a run of river plant with three Kaplan units, a combined swallowing capacity of 180 cubic metres per second and a gross head of 20.55 m at a flow of 60 cubic metres per second. The reservoir holds about 1.15 million cubic metres of useful storage, the permitted water level fluctuation is 1.5 m, and the catchment is 1,632 square kilometres. Average annual generation is about 105 GWh. In July 2022 the plant stopped generating entirely because of the low flow of the Soča. The operator brochure records that a reconstruction is planned for after 2025.

structure.built: 1984, in operation since 15 November 1984. Construction began in 1978.

properties.name: HE Zlatoličje
properties.zag_role: Non-shrink cements in the construction (introduced by ZRMK), technical observation of the dam
properties.description: ZAG's 2024 book states that ZRMK, the predecessor of ZAG, introduced non-shrink cements in the construction of HE Zlatoličje, and lists Zlatoličje and Melje among the Drava dams under ZAG technical observation. The plant works from a diversion canal rather than directly on the Drava channel. ZAG also lists third party quality control of the materials used in the upgrading of the Zlatoličje HPP, for Dravske elektrarne Maribor, 2006 to 2009.
properties.hist: HE Zlatoličje was the first canal type plant built in the former state. Water is taken from the Drava at the Melje weir in Maribor and carried 17.2 km along a trapezoidal intake canal, largely on embankment, to the powerhouse near Zlatoličje, then returned to the Drava through a 6.2 km outflow canal cut deep into the ground. Between 2007 and 2013 both turbines and both generators were replaced along with the primary and secondary electrical equipment and the control systems, all six gates of the Melje weir were raised, and the dam and spillway wall were structurally reinforced. The replacement runner fitted to unit 2 has a diameter of 5,894 mm and a mass of 96 tonnes. Installed flow rose from 450 to 530 cubic metres per second and installed capacity rose by 12 MW. The small plant MHE Melje, running on the ecological minimum flow, entered service in January 2009.

properties.hist: HE Vuhred is a run of river plant on the Drava in the municipality of Radlje ob Dravi, the third in the chain from the Austrian border. Two units entered service in 1956 and a third followed in 1958, giving three Kaplan turbines of 24.1 MW each. The design flow is 550 cubic metres per second and the head is 17.41 m. The weir has four spillway fields, each 17 m wide, with a maximum discharge capacity of 5,800 cubic metres per second. The reservoir extends 13.1 km at full supply level and holds 10.3 million cubic metres, of which 2.2 million are usable for generation. During the refurbishment the supplier replaced the entire stator winding of generator 3 because the original bars, made to a different technology, overheated. The plant now runs without permanent staff on site.

properties.name: Sveti Križ Bay Cliff
properties.zag_role: Rockfall investigation and slope characterisation
properties.description: ZAG investigated a coastal rockfall of roughly 2,000 cubic metres from 2020 to 2023, within research project J1-2477, combining geological mapping, geodetic remote sensing and geomechanical laboratory testing of samples taken from the cliff. The University of Ljubljana reports this work as part of the project on erosion of the coastal flysch cliffs with risk assessment.
properties.hist: The Strunjan cliff is the highest and the longest flysch sea cliff on the Adriatic, rising to about 80 m at Cape Ronek and running roughly 4 km between Capes Kane and Ronek. It is the longest stretch of undeveloped natural shoreline on the 130 km of coast between Grado in Italy and Savudrija in Croatia. The rock is middle Eocene flysch, a rhythmic alternation of conglomerate, sandstone, mudstone, marlstone and occasional limestone megabeds laid down in deep water about 40 million years ago and later folded and uplifted. Waves cut notches at the base until the overlying sandstone and limestone beds break away, while rain, sun and wind break up the upper face, and the park authority states that the cliff retreats inland at roughly one centimetre a year. Rockfall is frequent and documented: about 2,000 cubic metres of flysch collapsed in the bay of Sveti Križ at the end of December 2019 and blocks of one to six tonnes fell in the bay of Sveti Križ in August 2023. The cliff, its vegetated crest and a 200 m belt of sea below it are protected as a nature reserve inside the Strunjan Landscape Park.

properties.name: Sitarjevec Mine
properties.zag_role: Characterisation of mine ochre as a pigment
properties.description: ZAG characterised the yellow limonite mud that forms in the mine and assessed it as a source of natural pigment for artistic and textile use. The work is an example of the institute's materials side rather than its structures side.
properties.hist: Sitarjevec is a polymetallic mine on the hill above Litija that worked lead and mercury ores and later zinc, copper, iron bearing material and barite, the choice following market demand and price. Mining on the hill goes back to prehistory, the earliest written evidence is the 1537 gravestone of the mining master Cristof Bruckherschmidt, and a smelter operated from 1881. Work stopped at the end of July 1965 because the remaining ore was too poor, the recovery technology outdated and silicosis widespread among the miners, and the adits were then blasted shut. After 2000 limonite speleothems were discovered in the abandoned workings, iron and manganese formations regarded as among the finest in Europe, some of which grow up to 5 cm a year. The municipality rehabilitated part of the mine between 2017 and 2019, creating 632 m of museum routes, and guided tours began in December 2017 with the Glavni rov opening on 22 April 2021.

properties.name: ZAG
properties.zag_role: Slovenian National Building and Civil Engineering Institute
properties.description: Origins in 1949, operating in its present form since 1 April 1995. 254 staff at the end of 2023, five departments, the Laboratory for Metrology and three notified-body services under the Construction Products Regulation. Home of SiWIM bridge weigh-in-motion and of the BrAId project applying machine learning to B-WIM data quality.
properties.hist: The institute traces its origin to 18 July 1949, when the first building and civil engineering institute in Slovenia was set up with twelve staff. It was renamed the Institute for Testing and Research in Materials and Structures, ZRMK Ljubljana, in 1952, by which time it had grown to 150 employees and had its own building on Dimičeva. After independence the government reorganised ZRMK in 1994 and 1995 and split it into two bodies. ZAG was registered on 17 March 1995 and began operating on 1 April 1995 as a governmental non profit research institute, a status that lets it act as an independent third party in testing and certification. It is organised into five departments, Materials, Building Physics, Fire Safe Sustainable Built Environment, Structures, and Geotechnics and Infrastructure, together with the Laboratory for Metrology, the Certification Service and the Service for Technical Assessment and Approvals.

properties.name: ZAG Fire Laboratory Logatec
properties.zag_role: Fire resistance and reaction to fire testing
properties.description: Opened in 2022 and staffed by around twenty five people. It carries out fire resistance and reaction to fire testing on construction products and assemblies, including large scale furnace tests that the older Gameljne facility could not accommodate.
properties.hist: ZAG opened its Fire Laboratory at Obrtna cona 35 in Logatec on 2 September 2022, describing it as the largest facility of its kind in this part of Europe. The building has 3,421.70 square metres of gross floor area and holds two large furnaces with an exhaust gas cleaning plant. Specimens can be tested from microscale up to 4 m by 8 m. The declared project cost was 9,227,065.78 euros excluding VAT, made up of 1,660,554.40 euros from the state budget through the ministry, 4,305,077.38 euros of ZAG funds, 2,896,586.00 euros of ERDF funds through InnoRenew and 364,848.00 euros from ARRS, with the total including equipment reported as close to 11 million euros. Fire resistance testing covers non load bearing walls, ceilings and suspended facades, load bearing walls, ceilings, roofs, beams, columns, balconies and stairs, fire and smoke doors and windows with their hardware, protective systems for concrete, steel and timber, ventilation ducts, fire dampers, cable systems and smoke and heat control systems.

The unit occupies a renovated three storey building of 480 square metres, with offices and laboratories taking the whole of the ground floor, and the investment was about 300,000 euros. properties.name: Cestel d.o.o.
properties.zag_role: Industrial partner on bridge weigh-in-motion work
properties.description: SiWIM grew out of the weigh-in-motion research ZAG has run since the 1990s. Cestel supplies and operates the systems, and is a partner alongside ZAG in the BRIDGITISE doctoral network and on the Tomačevo bridge installation.
properties.hist: Cestel d.o.o. is at Špruha 32 in Trzin and states more than thirty years of experience in bridge weigh in motion measurement, traffic analysis and bridge assessment. Its product is SiWIM, presented as the first fully portable high speed weigh in motion system, which uses strain gauge sensors to collect data on heavy goods vehicles and on the bridge at the same time. The system measures gross vehicle weight, axle loads, axle spacing and speed, can be installed in less than a day without closing the road, and delivers data through web applications. The International Society for Weigh in Motion records that Cestel introduced SiWIM in 1999. The system is used for maintenance planning, for vehicle preselection in enforcement, and for bridge assessment.

properties.name: InnoRenew CoE
properties.zag_role: Partner institute, ZAG is a founding partner
properties.description: Set up under the Horizon 2020 teaming action with ZAG among the partners. It works on renewable building materials and healthy indoor environments. Friderik Knez led ZAG's side of the project from 2017-2022.
properties.hist: InnoRenew CoE is at Livade 6a in Izola and works on renewable materials and sustainable building. Its two distinguishing fields are wood modification and restorative environmental and ergonomic design. A consortium of ten partners led by the University of Primorska submitted the proposal to Horizon 2020 in 2016, and ZAG was one of the core partners. The Horizon 2020 Teaming operation was valued at 14,996,025.00 euros including tax, with national co financing of about 39 million euros, giving a total of about 54 million euros. Since a court decision of 29 July 2025, InnoRenew CoE has been an independent department of the UP Andrej Marušič Institute at the University of Primorska. Over eight and a half years it had run 96 publicly funded projects worth 15.78 million euros together with industry projects worth 2.81 million euros.

properties.hist: UL FGG is at Jamova cesta 2 in Ljubljana. Civil engineering teaching in Slovenia began in 1919, when the Department of Civil Engineering started courses at the Technical Faculty. The faculty passed through several reorganisations, becoming a department within the Technical Faculty in 1954 and part of the Faculty of Architecture, Civil and Geodetic Engineering in 1957, before becoming an independent member of the University of Ljubljana on 1 January 1995. It has three departments, Civil Engineering with twelve units including the chairs of structural and earthquake engineering, of mechanics and of geotechnical engineering, Geodetic Engineering with five chairs, and Environmental Civil Engineering. It also runs the Institute of Structural Engineering, Earthquake Engineering and Construction IT, the Water Management Institute, and hydraulic and structural testing laboratories.

properties.name: Čatež Bridge over the Sava
properties.zag_role: Combined earthquake and flood vulnerability assessment
properties.description: Within the CROSScade project the bridge was selected as the most critical of seven bridges studied, two of them in Slovenia near the Brežice hydropower plant and the others near Zagreb. Reasons given were its role on a key regional route, the lack of adequate scour protection and a design that predates modern performance-based seismic provisions. The first half of the bridge was modelled in Midas Civil and OpenSeesPy with soil-structure interaction, and fragility curves were derived for sequential ground shaking, flood loading and local pier scour.
properties.hist: The Čatež bridge carries a regional road across the Sava close to the Slovenia to Croatia border. It is a 12 span prestressed reinforced concrete girder bridge, 359.8 m long, designed in the mid 1970s. It is divided into four brake units by expansion joints. The intermediate piers are pairs of 1.2 m circular columns on bored piles, while piers 5 and 9 are transverse reinforced concrete walls on a pile cap with six inclined piles.
facts: non-linear time-history, earthquake followed by flood and scour

structure.carries: Regional road
structure.typ: Prestressed reinforced concrete girder bridge on circular column piers and two wall piers

properties.name: Maribor circular economy pilot sites
properties.zag_role: Demonstration of secondary raw materials in urban construction and urban soil
properties.description: CINDERELA, coordinated by ZAG, established a pilot production plant for construction products from waste in Maribor, planned a one storey demonstration building made with recycled aggregates and recycled soil, and carried out preliminary geotechnical investigation for revitalising a degraded area. URBAN SOIL 4 FOOD, an Urban Innovative Actions project led by the City of Maribor with ZAG as a partner, tested a pilot system for producing certified urban soil from city waste and used it in community gardens.
properties.hist: Maribor hosted Slovenian pilots of two circular economy projects in which ZAG took part. The CINDERELA pilots cover production of construction products from non-hazardous construction and other waste, a demonstration building with green concrete and recycled aggregates, and geotechnical works with secondary raw materials on a degraded area. The URBAN SOIL 4 FOOD project used excavated materials and biological waste from the city to produce standardised soil for urban gardens.
facts: one storey, green concrete with recycled aggregates

properties.name: National and University Library
properties.zag_role: Condition assessment of Plečnik’s façade before renovation
properties.description: Interdisciplinary survey of the façade (concrete, brick, stone and steel reinforcement) commissioned by NUK with the Institute for the Protection of Cultural Heritage of Slovenia. Methods reported: ultrasonic tomography, ground-penetrating radar, 3D micro-tomography, analyses of brick and joint mortars, and testing of conservation materials. ZAG reported in December 2025 that the research was in progress to provide the expert basis for a full renovation of the façade.
